Bentley|Barry J. Bentley|Raymond B. Bentley}} | hq_location = {{nowrap|[[Exton, Pennsylvania]], U.S.}} | website = {{URL|bentley.com}} }} '''Bentley Systems, Incorporated''' is a US-based [[software development]] company that develops, manufactures, licenses, sells and supports [[computer software]] and services for the [[design]], [[construction]], and operation of [[infrastructure]] globally. The company's software serves the building, plant, civil, and geospatial markets in the areas of [[architecture]], [[engineering]], [[construction]] (AEC) and operations. Their software products are used to design, engineer, build, and operate large constructed assets such as [[roadway]]s, [[railway]]s, [[bridge]]s, [[buildings]], [[industrial plant]]s, [[power plant]]s, and [[public utility|utility]] networks. Bentley Systems is headquartered in [[Exton, Pennsylvania]], United States, but reports development, sales and other departments in 45 countries. In 2025, the company reported revenue of $1.5 billion in 189 countries. ==History== {{plain image with caption|Bentley Systems logo.svg|Retired logo and wordmark}} Keith A. Bentley and Barry J. Bentley founded Bentley Systems in 1984.Section 10: CAD/CAM/CAE/CADD: [https://design.osu.edu/carlson/history/lesson10.html Section 10: CAD/CAM/CAE/CADD] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160404022755/http://design.osu.edu/carlson/history/lesson10.html |date=April 4, 2016 }}, accessdate: September 14, 2016 In an interview with trade publication Geo Week News, Keith Bentley recounted how he had previously developed CAD software while working as a programmer at DuPont.{{Cite web|url=https://www.geoweeknews.com/blogs/bentley-systems-keith-bentley-retirement-interview-cto-co-founder|title=A conversation with Bentley Systems co-founder Keith Bentley | Geo Week News|website=www.geoweeknews.com}} After retaining rights to this software, he joined his brother Barry's chemistry software startup, and they later pivoted to the CAD software market. Their brothers Greg, Scott, and Ray later joined the company, which relocated to Pennsylvania.{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.com/bentley-goes-public-finally/|title=Bentley Goes Public- Finally|date=October 5, 2020}} They introduced the commercial version of PseudoStation in 1985, which allowed users of [[Intergraph]]'s [[VAX]] systems to use low-cost [[graphics terminal]]s to view and modify the designs on their Intergraph IGDS (Interactive Graphics Design System) installations.{{cite book|author=David E. Weisberg|title=The Engineering Design Revolution : The People, Companies and Computer Systems That Changed Forever the Practice of Engineering|url=http://www.cadhistory.net/10%20Bentley.pdf|access-date=September 12, 2016|year=2008|pages=10â€“1|archive-date=March 7, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220307174221/http://cadhistory.net/10%20Bentley.pdf|url-status=dead}} An [[MS-DOS]] version of MicroStation was introduced in 1986.{{cite book|author=Ranjit S. Sahai|title=Teach yourself MicroStation J|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nfoTJ9S_u-AC|access-date=September 14, 2016|date=June 1999|publisher=Alpha Press|isbn=978-1-892658-00-5|page=10}} In April 2002, Bentley filed for an [[initial public offering]],{{Cite web |title= Form S-1: Registration Statement |date= April 23, 2002 |publisher= United States Securities and Exchange Commission |url= https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1031308/000089322002000491/w59294s-1.htm |access-date= November 11, 2016 }} but it was withdrawn before taking effect.{{Cite web |title= Form RW: Registration Withdrawal Request |date= September 16, 2002 |publisher= United States Securities and Exchange Commission |url= https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1031308/000089322002001123/w59294wrw.txt |access-date= November 11, 2016 }} In November 2016, German-based [[Siemens]] announced it would pay about $76 million for a minority stake in Bentley, as well as invest in developing joint software with it.{{Cite news |title= Siemens invests $130 million in Bentley Systems, pre-IPO |work= Philly.Com |date= November 10, 2016 |author= Joseph N. DiStefano |url= http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/inq-phillydeals/Siemens-invests-70-million-in-Malvern-software-firm.html |access-date= November 11, 2016 }} In September 2020, Bentley Systems set terms of its IPO valuing the company at about $4.96 billion. The company would offer 10.75 million shares priced between $17 and $19 per share.{{Cite news|date=September 15, 2020|title=Software developer Bentley Systems aims for near $5 billion IPO valuation|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bentley-systems-ipo-idUSKBN2662ZK|access-date=September 16, 2020}}{{Cite web|last=Kilgore|first=Tomi|title=Bentley Systems sets IPO terms, to raise up to $204.3 million and be valued at nearly $5 billion|url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/bentley-systems-sets-ipo-terms-to-raise-up-to-2043-million-and-be-valued-at-nearly-5-billion-2020-09-15|access-date=September 16, 2020|website=MarketWatch|date=September 15, 2020 |language=en-US}} In 2023, the company reported that its annual 2022 revenue exceeded $1 billion.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1031308/000103130825000002/bsy-20241231.htm#ic737041303a94a84bbc963d0e9d92cd4_301|title=bsy-20241231|website=www.sec.gov}} Also in 2023, Keith Bentley retired from his Chief Technology role,{{Cite web|url=https://www.jonpeddie.com/news/a-first-for-longtime-bentley-systems/|title=A first for longtime Bentley Systems|date=July 1, 2024}} and Greg Bentley retired in March 2024.{{Cite web|url=https://diginomica.com/legacy-built-40-years-trust-learnings-greg-bentley-he-steps-down-ceo-bentley-systems|title=A legacy built on 40 years of trust - learnings from Greg Bentley as he steps down as CEO of Bentley Systems|date=March 25, 2024|website=diginomica.com}} In July 2024, Chief Operating Officer Nicholas Cumins became the first non-family member to lead the company as CEO. ==Products== Bentley Systems sells software for infrastructure modeling, simulation, construction, operations, and analytics. The company's Seequent subsidiary sells geological and geophysical modeling and analysis software.{{Cite web|url=https://aecmag.com/digital-twin/bentley-systems-to-acquire-seequent-for-1-05-billion/|title=Bentley Systems to acquire Seequent for $1.05 billion|first=Greg|last=Corke|date=March 12, 2021}} Principle offerings include: ===Engineering and simulation applications=== {{main|MicroStation}} [[MicroStation]] is computer-aided design (CAD) software used in infrastructure projects. It provides tools for drafting, modeling, and visualization. The platform includes features for referencing external files, conducting design reviews, and integrating geospatial data.{{Cite web|url=https://www.slashgear.com/1958743/bentley-software-explained-is-it-same-as-microstation-bim/|title=What Is Bentley Software & Is It The Same As MicroStation?|first=Joseph|last=Chidi|date=September 7, 2025|website=SlashGear}} The company also provides Open applications for modelling and simulation based on MicroStation technology, designed to support workflows across infrastructure sectors. Modeling applications include:{{Cite web|url=https://zweiglist.com/open-applications-extend-bentleys-design-engineering-and-analysis-portfolio/|title=Open applications extend Bentley’s design engineering and analysis portfolio - Zweig List|website=zweiglist.com/}} * OpenRoads - for transportation infrastructure design * OpenRail - for railway design * OpenBridge Designer - for bridge design * OpenBuildings Designer, including Openbuildings Station Designer - for architectural and building design * OpenFlows Flood - for hydraulic and hydrologic modeling, analysis, design & operation * OpenPlant - for process plant design and operations * OpenUtilities - for electrical systems and substations design * OpenSite Designer - for modeling and analysis of site design project Open simulation applications include: * [[STAAD]] - structural analysis and design software{{Cite web|url=https://futureiot.tech/standing-with-staad-revolutionising-structural-design/|title=Standing With STAAD: Revolutionising Structural Design - FutureIoT|date=February 1, 2024}} * AutoPipe - pipe stress analysis software{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/bentley-systems-releases-update-for-autopipe-connect-edition-2017-08-11|title=Bentley Systems releases update for AutoPIPE Connect edition|first=Ilan|last=Solomons|website=Engineering News}} * Power Line Systems (PLS) - for analysis and simulation of overhead electric power transmission lines and their structures{{Cite web|url=https://www.energetica-india.net/articles/exo-inc-stabilises-damaged-grid-tower-supporting-critical-power-source-to-central-missouri|title=Exo Inc. Stabilises Damaged Grid Tower Supporting Critical Power Source to Central Missouri|first=Energética|last=India|date=May 15, 2025|website=Energetica India Magazine, India Energy News, Renewable Energy News, Conventional Power Generation, Companies Guide...}} ===Bentley Infrastructure Cloud === Bentley Infrastructure Cloud is an integrated online application that combines [[ProjectWise]] software for project delivery, SYNCHRO for construction management, and AssetWise for asset operations.{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.com/bentley-introduces-infrastructure-cloud-connect/|title=Bentley introduces Infrastructure Cloud Connect|first=Puja|last=Mitra|date=October 16, 2025}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.heavyquipmag.com/2023/02/16/bentley-systems-to-showcase-its-synchro-cloud-solution-at-conexpo-2023-2/|title=Bentley Systems to Showcase Its SYNCHRO Cloud Solution at CONEXPO 2023|date=February 16, 2023}} It provides a unified data environment to improve collaboration. ProjectWise is information management software used to manage CAD, BIM, geospatial and project data from a variety of vendors.{{Cite web|url=https://gfxspeak.com/archives/bentley-project-management/|title=Bentley takes project management to the cloud|date=September 26, 2014}} AssetWise is asset lifecycle information management (ALIM) software used to manage project assets including documents, tags, associated metadata, and 3D models.{{Cite web|url=https://www.geoconnexion.com/news/bp-selects-assetwise-lifecycle-information-management-and-assetwise-reliability-as-standard-for-information-management-and-asset-integrity|title=bp Selects AssetWise Lifecycle Information Management and AssetWise Reliability as Standard for Information Management and Asset Integrity|website=GeoConnexion}} The company's SYNCHRO software is used for 4D construction planning, scheduling, and productivity tracking, for teams on construction sites and in the office.{{Cite web|url=https://aecmag.com/features/bentley-synchro/|title=Bentley Synchro|first=Martyn|last=Day|date=February 21, 2019}} ===Asset Analytics=== Bentley's Asset Analytics portfolio applies artificial intelligence and digital twin workflows to improve infrastructure monitoring and maintenance.{{Cite web|url=https://emag.directindustry.com/2024/10/16/partnership-with-google-opensite-and-carbon-analysis-key-takeaways-from-bentley-systems-year-in-infrastructure-event/|title=Key Takeaways from Bentley Systems’ Year in Infrastructure Event|first=Camille|last=Rustici|date=October 16, 2024}} The product integrates data captured with physical devices such as IoT sensors, drones, and dashcams, with digital twins to create a comprehensive view of infrastructure such as bridges, dams, and large transportation networks. The portfolio includes Blyncsy, AI-powered software that analyzes roadway conditions using image date and machine learning.
===Seequent=== Bentley's Seequent subsidiary develops and sells 3D modeling and analysis software for the geosciences, mining, civil engineering, and energy industries.{{Cite web|url=https://www.canadianminingjournal.com/featured-article/how-geoscience-software-flipped-the-mining-industry-on-its-head/|title=How geoscience software flipped the mining industry on its head|date=May 9, 2025}} Seequent's portfolio includes Leapfrog for 3D geological modeling and visualization, GeoStudio for geotechnical and geoenvironmental analysis, and Geosoft for 3D earth modeling and geoscience data management. Seequent's Evo cloud platform integrates geoscience data from Seequent and third-party applications into one platform.{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.com/seequent-launches-evo-cloud-platform-for-geoscience-collaboration/|title=Seequent launches Evo cloud platform for geoscience collaboration|first=Puja|last=Mitra|date=March 6, 2025}} ===iTwin Platform=== Bentley's iTwin Platform is a cloud-native platform designed to enable [[digital twin]] workflows for infrastructure.{{cn|date=May 2026}} Digital twins representations allow customers to simulate physical assets such as roads, bridges, and buildings, while integrating engineering models, geospatial data, and enterprise information.{{cn|date=May 2026}} The iTwin platform integrates with 3D Tiles, through Bentley's acquisition of Cesium, the creator of the 3D Tiles community standard.{{Cite web|url=https://www.enr.com/articles/59240-bentley-buys-cesium-geospatial-information-and-digital-twin-platform|title=Bentley Buys Cesium, Geospatial Information and Digital Twin Platform | Engineering News-Record|website=www.enr.com}} This allows developers to combine 3D geospatial data with digital asset data to create scalable digital twins.{{Cite web|url=https://www.geoweeknews.com/news/bentley-cesium-acquistion-geospatial-3d-visualization-digital-twins|title=Bentley Systems Acquires 3D Geospatial Platform Provider Cesium|website=www.geoweeknews.com}} ===Cesium === Bentley Systems Cesium software is an open platform for building 3D geospatial applications.{{Cite web|url=https://aecmag.com/features/geo-whiz-bentley-to-acquire-cesium/|title=Geo whiz: Bentley acquires Cesium|first=Martyn|last=Day|date=September 22, 2024}} Cesium also created the 3D Tiles community standard, an [[Open Geospatial Consortium]] (OGC) standard for streaming large 3D data sets.{{Cite web|url=https://www.interesting.us/|title=OGC adopts 3D Tiles as Community Standard | WITI Recommends|website=www.interesting.us}} In 2025, Bentley started integrating its iTwin Platform with Cesium, beginning with adding iTwin Capture reality modeling services to Cesium.{{Cite web|url=https://www.traffictechnologytoday.com/news/infrastructure/bentley-adds-reality-modeling-to-cesium-platform.html|title=Bentley adds reality modeling to Cesium platform|first=Helen|last=Norman|date=October 16, 2025}} The company also announced 3D tile integration with its MicroStation product.{{Cite web|url=https://www.geoweeknews.com/news/bentley-systems-bolsters-cesium-with-reality-modeling-capabilities-brings-geospatial-context-to-infrastructure-engineering|title=Bentley Systems Bolsters Cesium with Reality Modeling Capabilities, Brings Geospatial Context to Infrastructure Engineering | Geo Week News|website=www.geoweeknews.com}} ==Artificial intelligence== Bentley invests in artificial intelligence and machine learning, through internal research and development, and acquisitions, including AIworx (2018) and Blyncsy (2023).{{Cite web|url=https://aecmag.com/digital-twin/bentley-systems-the-promise-of-data-freedom/|title=Bentley Systems: the promise of data freedom|first=Greg|last=Corke|date=October 14, 2024}} Bentley software, including OpenRoads, OpenRail, and ProjectWise, includes the Bentley Copilot, a context-aware AI assistant that guides users through workflows, surfaces relevant documents, and can modify 3D models.{{Cite web|url=https://www.enr.com/articles/61673-bentley-unveils-platform-upgrades-redoubles-ai-investment|title=Bentley Unveils Platform Upgrades; Redoubles AI Investment | Engineering News-Record|website=www.enr.com}} OpenSite+ is Bentley's first application to incorporate generative AI. It also offers AI-driven variants of its SYNCHRO (SYNCHRO+) and Substation (Substation+) applications.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bim-world.de/bentley-systems-advances-infrastructure-ai-with-new-applications-and-industry-collaboration|title=Bentley Systems Advances Infrastructure AI with New Applications and Industry Collaboration|first=B. I. M.|last=World|date=November 20, 2025}} In May 2026, Bentley Systems published the STAAD MCP server to the open [[Model Context Protocol]] (MCP) Registry. This development connects AI agents directly with STAAD.Pro, allowing different AI systems to access the application's structural validation functions and data.{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.com/siemens-and-xometry-to-bring-instant-quoting-dfm-analysis-to-designcenter/|title=Siemens and Xometry to bring instant quoting, DFM analysis to Designcenter|first=Michael|last=Alba|date=May 12, 2026}} ==Operations== Bentley is headquartered in Exton, Pennsylvania. Nicholas Cumins is the company's CEO. The company reports 5,800 employees in 45 countries, and in 2025 reported $1.5 Billion in revenue in 189 countries.{{cite web|url=https://investors.bentley.com/node/13466/html|title=Bentley Systems 2025 Form 10-K|date=February 26, 2026|accessdate=June 12, 2026}} ==Partnerships== *Microsoft - extract:
Bentley Systems, Incorporated is a US-based software development company that develops, manufactures, licenses, sells and supports computer software and services for the design, construction, and operation of infrastructure globally. The company's software serves the building, plant, civil, and geospatial markets in the areas of architecture, engineering, construction (AEC) and operations. Their software products are used to design, engineer, build, and operate large constructed assets such as roadways, railways, bridges, buildings, industrial plants, power plants, and utility networks.
Bentley Systems is headquartered in Exton, Pennsylvania, United States, but reports development, sales and other departments in 45 countries. In 2025, the company reported revenue of $1.5 billion in 189 countries.
